solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Divulge receiving phosphorus atom component

parts.note: P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: A scientist leaks what happens when phosphorus picks up a particle.
explanation.walkthrough: LET ON splits after LE to take the P. A lepton is a light particle such as the electron.
explanation.definitionFit: Leptons, including electrons, are among the particles that make up an atom.

clue.text: Source of light wasted, needing measure of current and power introduced

parts.note: the amp is the unit of electric current
P = power, as in physics formulae

explanation.surface: An electrician complains that a wasteful light needs more current and power.
explanation.walkthrough: The electrical words all look like they belong to the definition, but only 'Source of light' does; current and power are building bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by function: the post carries the street lamp, so the whole thing is loosely where the light comes from.

clue.text: Not entirely weak joke

explanation.surface: A comedian's gag falls a little flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weak joke' reads as one phrase, but 'weak' is wordplay and 'joke' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun is a joke that plays on a word's two meanings.

clue.text: Work hard, securing right answer for deprived children

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast

parts.note: ANS is the usual abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Someone toils to find the right solution for poor children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work hard' reads as one verb, toil, but splits into OP and H.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain gloss: the deprivation meant is the loss of parents, not poverty, which the surface suggests.

clue.text: Former student tired having gone round front of college block

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: having gone round says the word for tired encircles the following letter
front of picks the first letter of college

parts.note: the word college, whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A weary old boy walks round the front of his former college building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'block' looks like a building, but it is a hindrance. 'front of' gives C from college, which STALE (tired) 'having gone round' surrounds, after OB.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance that stands in your way blocks progress, so a barrier and a block are synonyms.

clue.text: Something to help EV driver, finally, after accusation of assault?

indicators.note: after says the single letter comes behind the long phrase

parts.note: a battery charge is an accusation of the crime of assault, battery

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of driver

parts.note: the word driver, whose last letter is taken

explanation.surface: An electric car's driver ends up facing an assault charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' looks part of the definition, but 'finally' just takes its last letter, R, placed 'after' BATTERY CHARGE. EV is short for electric vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that tops up the cells of an electric vehicle with power assists it, so it is a helpful piece of kit.

clue.text: Conflicted about love, is upset in wrench

indicators.note: about says the word for conflicted is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: torn means conflicted, unable to decide

indicators.note: upset says the little word is is turned over, read in reverse

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone torn over a love affair is in distress, wrenched by emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses IS to SI, which with O (love) goes inside TORN, 'about' signalling the wrap. 'wrench' is a twist, not grief.
explanation.definitionFit: A twisting force applied to an object is a wrench in mechanical terms, as in twisting a bar.

clue.text: Study more than half of traffic — minimum levels in set-ups around roadworks

parts.note: to con is to study closely
lows = minimum levels, as in record lows

explanation.surface: A report studies traffic slowing to a crawl near roadworks.
explanation.walkthrough: A contraflow is the British arrangement where traffic is moved onto the opposite carriageway to pass roadworks.
explanation.definitionFit: Contraflows are traffic arrangements set up to get vehicles round roadworks.

clue.text: Catch new music, say, turning up in recording

indicators.note: in says the other pieces are placed inside the word for recording

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: turning up, in a down clue, says the word for music is read from bottom to top

parts.note: music is an example of an art

explanation.surface: Someone hears a new piece of rap music turning up on a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'music, say' is ART, not RAP: 'turning up' gives TRA, which follows N (new) 'in' EP (recording).
explanation.definitionFit: To snare or trap someone is to catch them, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Loin meat cleric misrepresented as spam etc

indicators.note: the letters are presented wrongly, rearranged

explanation.surface: Loin meat passed off as Spam, the tinned pork, with a clergyman involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Spam the tinned meat sits comfortably beside loin meat, but here spam is junk messages.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam and similar messages arrive by electronic mail.

clue.text: Chap turned up in clutches of fidgety tailor, one busy with their hands?

indicators.note: in clutches of says the reversed word sits inside the jumbled letters that hold it
fidgety suggests restless movement, so the letters of tailor are rearranged
turned says the word up is reversed

explanation.surface: A man shows up in the grip of a restless tailor, who is all hands.
explanation.walkthrough: After MAN, 'turned' gives PU from up, held 'in clutches of' ILATOR, the letters of TAILOR made 'fidgety'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who handles or operates things skilfully by hand, like a chiropractor or puppeteer, works with their fingers.

clue.text: New opponent in game, one easily confused?

parts.note: in tag, whoever is 'it' chases everyone else. The same letters also run on unbroken across neighbouring clue words, a coincidence of the pieces sitting side by side; the setter gives no hidden-word signal.

explanation.surface: A new rival in a game is baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a nit is a dim person, a nitwit; the question mark admits that the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A British colloquial sense: short for nitwit, a dimwit, and the question mark owns up to describing rather than defining.

clue.text: Expert's account defending India is unimaginative

parts.note: India is I in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A consultant's report on India is judged dull.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S is used as letters: PRO'S gives PROS.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: prosaic began as 'like prose' and came to mean dull and matter-of-fact.

clue.text: Historic corruption? Creative interpretation of events dismissing pressure

parts.note: a new slant, an original spin, on events

explanation.surface: Press officers spin a scandal from long ago without applying pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: Original sin is the corruption inherited from Adam's fall; 'historic' with a question mark stretches that to the first sin in history.
explanation.definitionFit: Original sin is the inherited moral corruption dating from the Fall.

clue.text: Country's anger reflected curtailment of party, perhaps

definitions.note: Country's reads as country is, the 's joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: reflected says the word for anger is read backwards, as in a mirror
curtailment of says the word for a party loses its last letter

parts.note: a treat, such as a party, is an example of an enjoyable outing

explanation.surface: A nation's fury mirrored in a party cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns IRE into ERI; 'curtailment of' trims TREAT to TREA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Horn of Africa state on the Red Sea coast is a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Versatile tool, swanky, misfires when deployed

indicators.note: the letters are spread out and rearranged

explanation.surface: A flashy gadget keeps failing whenever it is put to use.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a sneer at a posh gizmo; nothing in it points to Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss Army knife folds many tools into one handle.

clue.text: A lot of publicity and a lot of attention may be mesmerising

indicators.note: most of HYPE: drop the last letter
most of NOTICE: drop the last letter

explanation.surface: Heavy press coverage and public attention can hold people spellbound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' reads as quantity, but here it is a trimming instruction: most of the word, not much of the thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypnotic means mesmerising, holding the attention as if in a trance.

clue.text: Exaggerate problems in column, supported by two articles, and leave city

parts.note: a pile is a column driven into the ground to support a building
on = in, as in 'on the team'

explanation.surface: A columnist, backed by a couple of pieces, overstates the city's woes and quits town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Problems in column' reads like newspaper troubles, but 'problems' closes the definition and 'in column' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To pile on the agony is to make a situation sound worse than it is.

clue.text: Authorise it during tender, $1000 being expended

indicators.note: something happening during another is within its span, so IT sits inside the word
money expended is spent and gone

parts.note: G = grand, a thousand dollars; removed

explanation.surface: Someone approves a bid in which a thousand dollars is spent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' tempts as a bid, which fits the money; it is actually the adjective, GENTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean granting someone a right to do or have something.

clue.text: Tech company in the vicinity of Cumbrian town

parts.note: Apple, the maker of the iPhone

explanation.surface: A technology firm sets up near a small town in the English Lakes.
explanation.walkthrough: Appleby-in-Westmorland is a market town in Cumbria, in north-west England, known for its horse fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a place name clued by its county, Cumbria in north-west England.

clue.text: What physio may apply before reserve comes off?

definitions.meaning: read straight, the treatment a physio puts on an injury: a bag of ice
a player's name ahead of the reserve's reads as ICE then BAG, since to bag is to reserve (bag a seat)

explanation.surface: A physiotherapist treats a player before the substitute leaves the field.
explanation.walkthrough: The sports surface hides a second reading: ICE is what a physio applies, and it comes before BAG, to reserve, as in bagging a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice bag is a bag of ice put on an injury to reduce swelling.

clue.text: Confused bloke clipped on the ear

parts.note: CHAP = bloke, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A dazed man has been cuffed round the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipped on the ear' is a British phrase for a light slap; here clipped trims CHAP and 'on the ear' becomes OTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaotic means in total disorder, confused.

clue.text: Persuades Earl to invest in reform of prison

indicators.note: to invest in says the earl's letter is put inside the reworked word
reform of says the letters of prison are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A nobleman is persuaded to put money into rebuilding a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform of' rearranges PRISON as ROPSIN, and 'to invest in' puts E (Earl) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax or enlist someone into joining a venture is to persuade them, an informal phrasal synonym.

clue.text: America getting behind baseball's foremost coach?

indicators.note: in an across answer, behind means later in the line
the foremost part of a word is its front, its first letter

explanation.surface: The USA rallies behind its leading baseball trainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a sports trainer after baseball; the question mark hints at the other coach, a road vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a coach is a long-distance bus.

clue.text: Setter cared about proprietary information

indicators.note: the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: The crossword setter was worried about protecting confidential details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' tempts you to write in ME or I, but here it is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade secret is information a business keeps to itself as its own property.

clue.text: Rent ready for reduction

indicators.note: for reduction says the word for ready is cut by one final letter

parts.note: ripe means ready, as fruit is

explanation.surface: A landlord says the rent is ready to be lowered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord, but it is a tear. 'for reduction' trims RIPE to its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent is a tear or split in fabric, which is what a tear is too.

clue.text: Taking extreme care with lady's clothing after spicy stuff

indicators.note: after says the outer letters come behind the spice
clothing says only the letters wrapped around the outside of the word are kept

parts.note: the word lady, the possessive tying it to clothing

explanation.surface: A woman dresses carefully after eating something spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' keeps the outside letters L and Y of lady, placed 'after' GINGER (spicy stuff).
explanation.definitionFit: Moving cautiously and delicately, as if afraid of breaking something, means doing it with great caution.

clue.text: Nothing in photo I took, seeing only what's close

indicators.note: 'nothing in photo' puts the zero within the picture's letters

parts.note: a photo I took is my pic

explanation.surface: A photographer admits the snapshot came out blank, being short-sighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Photo I took' is a paraphrase to be turned into first-person slang, the possessive plus the short word for picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone myopic is short-sighted, seeing clearly only what is near.
